statements.subject: server
statements.description: As soon as the target set is non-empty, a proxy MAY begin forwarding the request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy MAY process the set in any order.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY process multiple targets serially, allowing each client transaction to complete before starting the next.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY start client transactions with every target in parallel.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It also MAY arbitrarily divide the set into groups, processing the groups serially and processing the targets in each group in parallel.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The copy MUST initially contain all of the header fields from the received request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Fields not detailed in the processing described below MUST NOT be removed.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The copy SHOULD maintain the ordering of the header fields as in the received request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MUST NOT reorder field values with a common field name (See Section 7.3.1).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MUST NOT add to, modify, or remove the message body.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Request-URI in the copy's start line MUST be replaced with the URI for this target.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the URI contains any parameters not allowed in a Request-URI, they MUST be removed.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the copy contains a Max-Forwards header field, the proxy MUST decrement its value by one (1).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the copy does not contain a Max-Forwards header field, the proxy MUST add one with a field value, which SHOULD be 70.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the copy does not contain a Max-Forwards header field, the proxy MUST add one with a field value, which SHOULD be 70.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If this proxy wishes to remain on the path of future requests in a dialog created by this request (assuming the request creates a dialog), it MUST insert a Record-Route header field value into the copy before any existing Record-Route header field values, even if a Route header field is already present.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If this request is already part of a dialog, the proxy SHOULD insert a Record-Route header field value if it wishes to remain on the path of future requests in the dialog.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A proxy MAY insert a Record-Route header field value into any request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The URI placed in the Record-Route header field value MUST be a SIP or SIPS URI.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This URI MUST contain an lr parameter (see Section 19.1.1).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This URI MAY be different for each destination the request is forwarded to.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The URI SHOULD NOT contain the transport parameter unless the proxy has knowledge (such as in a private network) that the next downstream element that will be in the path of subsequent requests supports that transport.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The URI placed in the Record-Route header field MUST resolve to the element inserting it (or a suitable stand-in) when the server location procedures of [4] are applied to it, so that subsequent requests reach the same SIP element.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the Request-URI contains a SIPS URI, or the topmost Route header field value (after the post processing of bullet 6) contains a SIPS URI, the URI placed into the Record-Route header field MUST be a SIPS URI.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Furthermore, if the request was not received over TLS, the proxy MUST insert a Record-Route header field.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In a similar fashion, a proxy that receives a request over TLS, but generates a request without a SIPS URI in the Request-URI or topmost Route header field value (after the post processing of bullet 6), MUST insert a Record-Route header field that is not a SIPS URI.
statements.pre_cond: request.received_transport = TLS & forwarded_request_uri.scheme != SIPS & route_header.topmost.scheme != SIPS

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the URI placed in the Record-Route header field needs to be rewritten when it passes back through in a response, the URI MUST be distinct enough to locate at that time.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MAY include parameters in the Record-Route header field value.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a proxy needs to be in the path of any type of dialog (such as one straddling a firewall), it SHOULD add a Record-Route header field value to every request with a method it does not understand since that method may have dialog semantics.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A dialog-stateful proxy, for example, MAY refuse to accept future requests with that value in the Request-URI after the dialog has terminated.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Non-dialog-stateful proxies, of course, have no concept of when the dialog has terminated, but they MAY encode enough information in the value to compare it against the dialog identifier of future requests and MAY reject requests not matching that information.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Non-dialog-stateful proxies, of course, have no concept of when the dialog has terminated, but they MAY encode enough information in the value to compare it against the dialog identifier of future requests and MAY reject requests not matching that information.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Endpoints MUST NOT use a URI obtained from a Record-Route header field outside the dialog in which it was provided.

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: INVITE is the only such request in this specification, but extensions to the protocol MAY define others.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MAY add any other appropriate header fields to the copy at this point.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A proxy MAY have a local policy that mandates that a request visit a specific set of proxies before being delivered to the destination.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A proxy MUST ensure that all such proxies are loose routers.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This set MUST be pushed into the Route header field of the copy ahead of any existing values, if present.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the Route header field is absent, it MUST be added, containing that list of URIs.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the request has a Route header field, this alternative MUST NOT be used unless it is known that next hop proxy is a loose router.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, this approach MAY be used, but the Route insertion mechanism above is preferred for its robustness, flexibility, generality and consistency of operation.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Furthermore, if the Request-URI contains a SIPS URI, TLS MUST be used to communicate with that proxy.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the copy contains a Route header field, the proxy MUST inspect the URI in its first value.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If that URI does not contain an lr parameter, the proxy MUST modify the copy as follows:

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MUST place the Request-URI into the Route header field as the last value.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MUST then place the first Route header field value into the Request-URI and remove that value from the Route header field.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MAY have a local policy to send the request to a specific IP address, port, and transport, independent of the values of the Route and Request-URI.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Such a policy MUST NOT be used if the proxy is not certain that the IP address, port, and transport correspond to a server that is a loose router.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, this mechanism for sending the request through a specific next hop is NOT RECOMMENDED; instead a Route header field should be used for that purpose as described above.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the proxy has reformatted the request to send to a strict-routing element as described in step 6 above, the proxy MUST apply those procedures to the Request-URI of the request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, the proxy MUST apply the procedures to the first value in the Route header field, if present, else the Request-URI.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Independently of which URI is being used as input to the procedures of [4], if the Request-URI specifies a SIPS resource, the proxy MUST follow the procedures of [4] as if the input URI were a SIPS URI.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As described in [4], the proxy MUST attempt to deliver the message to the first tuple in that set, and proceed through the set in order until the delivery attempt succeeds.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For each tuple attempted, the proxy MUST format the message as appropriate for the tuple and send the request using a new client transaction as detailed in steps 8 through 10.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Thus, the branch parameter provided with the Via header field inserted in step 8 MUST be different for each attempt.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MUST insert a Via header field value into the copy before the existing Via header field values.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A proxy choosing to detect loops SHOULD create a branch parameter separable into two parts by the implementation.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The first part MUST satisfy the constraints of Section 8.1.1.7 as described above.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The value placed in this part of the branch parameter SHOULD reflect all of those fields (including any Route, Proxy-Require and Proxy-Authorization header fields).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If a proxy wishes to detect loops, the "branch" parameter it supplies MUST depend on all information affecting processing of a request, including the incoming Request-URI and any header fields affecting the request's admission or routing.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The request method MUST NOT be included in the calculation of the branch parameter.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: In particular, CANCEL and ACK requests (for non-2xx responses) MUST have the same branch value as the corresponding request they cancel or acknowledge.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the request will be sent to the next hop using a stream-based transport and the copy contains no Content-Length header field, the proxy MUST insert one with the correct value for the body of the request (see Section 20.14).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateful proxy MUST create a new client transaction for this request as described in Section 17.1 and instructs the transaction to send the request using the address, port and transport determined in step 7.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Timer C MUST be set for each client transaction when an INVITE request is proxied.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The timer MUST be larger than 3 minutes.
